merges.why: Both name an area chair's tier assignment that the reviews and meta-review do not argue for, so the split reflects where the chair put the tier, not the reviews; R18 is the case where the other committee's scores were near-identical, which is an instance of R31's unexplained tier, not a different mechanism.

Both name a meta-review whose account of its own committee's record was wrong (weaknesses dropped or reversed, reviewers' final positions or answered concerns misreported) with the recommendation resting on that inaccurate account.

Both name reviewers who never replied to the authors' response or joined the discussion, so scores whose basis the response had answered stood unrevised; R22 restricts this to one outlying reviewer, which changes who did it, not the mechanism.

Both name an area chair who counted every score at equal weight regardless of the reviewer's expertise, so less-informed reviewers' scores set the recommendation; R19 states it from the side of the expert passed over, R27 from the side of the non-experts counted in full.

reasoning: I compared every entry with the others at the level of mechanism. Near-neighbours kept apart: R10 (chair adopts an outlier's verdict) vs R21 (an outlier's score moves the mean) vs R28 (chair settles an even split), which differ in who acts and how; R03 (rebuttal outcome) vs R20 (concerns were answerable) vs R13 (unverified rebuttal evidence) vs R16 (damaging admission ignored), which name different causes of a differential rebuttal effect; R09 (unsure reviewers default to borderline scores) vs R27, since R09 is a reviewer's scoring behaviour, not the chair's weighting; R12 (unanimity read as grounds for a higher tier), which names a stated ground and so is not R31's tier with no grounds; R01 (chair's own reading) vs R31, which R31's absence of any argued reason excludes; R08 (one rating against its own text) vs R11 (calibration gap between committees); R15 (misread results) vs R30 (misread prior work); R24 (audience or venue fit) vs R32 (neighbouring-field framing) vs R36 (contribution-type standard); R04 (thin reviews) vs R33 (no engaged champion); R05 (concern raised by one committee) vs R06 (same concern weighted differently).
